requirements.quote:
A list of cipher suites which indicates the AEAD algorithm/HKDF
      hash pairs which the client supports.
requirements.condition: when a client offers cipher suites in ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: use the list to indicate the AEAD algorithm and HKDF hash pairs supported by the client
requirements.forbidden_behavior: offer a cipher suite pair the client does not support
requirements.why_checkable: The offered cipher-suite pairs can be compared with the client's enabled AEAD and hash capabilities.

requirements.quote:
A "supported_groups" (Section 4.2.7) extension which indicates the
      (EC)DHE groups which the client supports
requirements.condition: when a client sends supported_groups
requirements.required_behavior: list the (EC)DHE groups supported by the client
requirements.forbidden_behavior: identify an unsupported group as supported
requirements.why_checkable: The extension contents can be compared with the client's configured group support.

requirements.quote:
a "key_share"
      (Section 4.2.8) extension which contains (EC)DHE shares for some
      or all of these groups.
requirements.condition: when a client sends key_share together with supported_groups
requirements.required_behavior: include (EC)DHE shares only for some or all groups named by supported_groups
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include a key share for a group outside the client's supported_groups list
requirements.why_checkable: Each KeyShareEntry group can be checked for membership in the offered supported_groups set.

requirements.quote:
A "signature_algorithms" (Section 4.2.3) extension which indicates
      the signature algorithms which the client can accept.
requirements.condition: when a client sends signature_algorithms
requirements.required_behavior: list signature algorithms that the client can accept
requirements.forbidden_behavior: advertise a signature algorithm the client cannot accept
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised algorithms can be compared with the client's signature-verification capabilities.

requirements.quote:
A
      "signature_algorithms_cert" extension (Section 4.2.3) may also be
      added to indicate certificate-specific signature algorithms.
requirements.condition: when the client needs to indicate certificate-specific signature algorithms
requirements.required_behavior: encode those preferences in an optional signature_algorithms_cert extension
requirements.why_checkable: The optional extension's presence and declared certificate-specific purpose can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A "pre_shared_key" (Section 4.2.11) extension which contains a
      list of symmetric key identities known to the client
requirements.condition: when a client sends pre_shared_key
requirements.required_behavior: list symmetric key identities known to the client
requirements.forbidden_behavior: offer a symmetric key identity not known to the client
requirements.why_checkable: Offered identities can be checked against the client's PSK or ticket store.

requirements.quote:
a
      "psk_key_exchange_modes" (Section 4.2.9) extension which indicates
      the key exchange modes that may be used with PSKs.
requirements.condition: when a client offers PSKs
requirements.required_behavior: use psk_key_exchange_modes to identify the key-establishment modes permitted with those PSKs
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised PSK mode set is explicit and can be compared with later server selection.

requirements.quote:
If the server does not select a PSK, then the first three of these
   options are entirely orthogonal: the server independently selects a
   cipher suite, an (EC)DHE group and key share for key establishment,
   and a signature algorithm/certificate pair to authenticate itself to
   the client.
requirements.condition: the server does not select a PSK and proceeds with negotiation
requirements.required_behavior: select a cipher suite from the client's offered cipher-suite options
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select a cipher suite outside the client's offered options
requirements.why_checkable: The selected cipher suite can be tested for membership in the ClientHello offer.

requirements.quote:
If the server does not select a PSK, then the first three of these
   options are entirely orthogonal: the server independently selects a
   cipher suite, an (EC)DHE group and key share for key establishment,
   and a signature algorithm/certificate pair to authenticate itself to
   the client.
requirements.condition: the server does not select a PSK and proceeds with negotiation
requirements.required_behavior: select an (EC)DHE group and key share compatible with the client's group and key-share options
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select an incompatible (EC)DHE group or key share
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated group and share can be compared with ClientHello supported_groups and key_share.

requirements.quote:
If the server does not select a PSK, then the first three of these
   options are entirely orthogonal: the server independently selects a
   cipher suite, an (EC)DHE group and key share for key establishment,
   and a signature algorithm/certificate pair to authenticate itself to
   the client.
requirements.condition: the server does not select a PSK and authenticates with a certificate
requirements.required_behavior: select a signature algorithm and certificate pair acceptable under the client's signature options
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select an incompatible signature algorithm or certificate pair
requirements.why_checkable: The selected authentication pair can be checked against the ClientHello signature preferences.

requirements.quote:
If there is no overlap between the received
   "supported_groups" and the groups supported by the server, then the
   server MUST abort the handshake with a "handshake_failure" or an
   "insufficient_security" alert.
requirements.condition: the server does not select a PSK and the client's supported_groups have no overlap with the server's groups
requirements.required_behavior: abort the handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue a non-PSK handshake without a mutually supported group
requirements.error_behavior: send a handshake_failure or insufficient_security alert
requirements.why_checkable: A ClientHello with a disjoint group set can be used to observe termination and the permitted alert.

requirements.quote:
If the server selects a PSK, then it MUST also select a key
   establishment mode from the set indicated by the client's
   "psk_key_exchange_modes" extension
requirements.condition: the server selects a PSK
requirements.required_behavior: select a PSK key-establishment mode from the client's psk_key_exchange_modes set
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select a PSK mode the client did not indicate
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated PSK mode can be compared directly with the client's advertised mode set.

requirements.quote:
if the PSK can be used without (EC)DHE, then
   non-overlap in the "supported_groups" parameters need not be fatal
requirements.condition: the selected PSK can be used without (EC)DHE and client and server supported_groups do not overlap
requirements.required_behavior: permit PSK-only negotiation to proceed despite the group non-overlap
requirements.forbidden_behavior: unconditionally apply the non-PSK group-overlap failure rule
requirements.why_checkable: A PSK-only mode with disjoint group sets can verify that group non-overlap is not treated as inherently fatal.

requirements.quote:
If the server selects an (EC)DHE group and the client did not offer a
   compatible "key_share" extension in the initial ClientHello, the
   server MUST respond with a HelloRetryRequest (Section 4.1.4) message.
requirements.condition: the server selects an (EC)DHE group for which the initial ClientHello has no compatible key share
requirements.required_behavior: respond with HelloRetryRequest
requirements.forbidden_behavior: proceed directly with ServerHello using the missing share
requirements.why_checkable: A ClientHello without the selected group's share can verify that the server takes the retry path.

requirements.quote:
If PSK is being used, then the server will send a "pre_shared_key"
      extension indicating the selected key.
requirements.condition: the negotiated handshake uses a PSK
requirements.required_behavior: send a ServerHello pre_shared_key extension that identifies the selected key
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit the selected PSK indication from ServerHello
requirements.why_checkable: The ServerHello extension can be checked against the server's selected PSK identity.

requirements.quote:
When (EC)DHE is in use, the server will also provide a "key_share"
      extension.
requirements.condition: (EC)DHE is used for key establishment
requirements.required_behavior: provide a ServerHello key_share extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit key_share from ServerHello
requirements.why_checkable: ServerHello extension presence is directly observable for an (EC)DHE handshake.

requirements.quote:
If PSK is not being used, then (EC)DHE and
      certificate-based authentication are always used.
requirements.condition: PSK is not used in a TLS 1.3 handshake
requirements.required_behavior: use (EC)DHE key establishment
requirements.forbidden_behavior: complete the handshake without (EC)DHE
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated key-establishment path can be inspected for an (EC)DHE exchange.

requirements.quote:
If PSK is not being used, then (EC)DHE and
      certificate-based authentication are always used.
requirements.condition: PSK is not used in a TLS 1.3 handshake
requirements.required_behavior: use certificate-based authentication
requirements.forbidden_behavior: complete the handshake without certificate authentication
requirements.why_checkable: The authentication message path can be inspected for certificate-based authentication.

requirements.quote:
When authenticating via a certificate, the server will send the
      Certificate (Section 4.4.2) and CertificateVerify (Section 4.4.3)
      messages.
requirements.condition: the server authenticates via a certificate
requirements.required_behavior: send a Certificate message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit the Certificate message
requirements.why_checkable: The server's certificate-authentication flight can be checked for the Certificate message.

requirements.quote:
When authenticating via a certificate, the server will send the
      Certificate (Section 4.4.2) and CertificateVerify (Section 4.4.3)
      messages.
requirements.condition: the server authenticates via a certificate
requirements.required_behavior: send a CertificateVerify message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit the CertificateVerify message
requirements.why_checkable: The server's certificate-authentication flight can be checked for the CertificateVerify message.

requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.3 as defined by this document, either a PSK or
      a certificate is always used, but not both.
requirements.condition: for a TLS 1.3 authentication path defined by RFC 8446
requirements.required_behavior: use at least one of PSK authentication or certificate authentication
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use neither PSK nor certificate authentication
requirements.why_checkable: The selected authentication path can be classified as PSK or certificate based.

requirements.quote:
In TLS 1.3 as defined by this document, either a PSK or
      a certificate is always used, but not both.
requirements.condition: for a TLS 1.3 authentication path defined by RFC 8446
requirements.required_behavior: select only one of PSK authentication and certificate authentication
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use PSK authentication and certificate authentication together
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake traces can be checked for mutually exclusive authentication paths.

requirements.quote:
If the server is unable to negotiate a supported set of parameters
   (i.e., there is no overlap between the client and server parameters),
   it MUST abort the handshake with either a "handshake_failure" or
   "insufficient_security" fatal alert (see Section 6).
requirements.condition: there is no supported overlap between the client and server negotiation parameters
requirements.required_behavior: abort the handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue with an unsupported parameter set
requirements.error_behavior: send a fatal handshake_failure or insufficient_security alert
requirements.why_checkable: Disjoint parameter offers can be used to test fatal termination and the allowed alert codes.
